coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 (130–140 bpm), rolling terrain if possible. You're 46 days out and in taper; the 5.2-miler yesterday was solid but light. Today is Monday—stay in recovery mode. Your RHR is 62 (solid) and recovery score is 97/100, so you have room to move, but don't chase intensity. This is about maintaining leg turnover and aerobic confidence without chewing into glycogen or CNS reserves. Keep it conversational and relaxed.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You slept 11.65 hours with 96.4% efficiency—exceptional. That's a recovery surplus, not a deficit sign. Eat normally but lean toward carbs (oats, rice, pasta, fruit) at breakfast and lunch to top off glycogen after yesterday's vert work. On the easy run today, carry 200–300 cal of carbs if it's over 90 minutes; otherwise, go fasted or minimal. Post-run, hit 30–40g protein + 60g carbs within 30 minutes to anchor recovery.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your sleep is elite right now—11+ hours with near-perfect efficiency. Don't fight it; your body is priming for the final push. Aim for 8–9 hours tonight (you don't need 11 every night, but this pace is fine). Foam roll the quads, calves, and IT band for 8–10 minutes post-run. Skip the ice bath; taper weeks benefit from normal core temperature recovery. Elevate legs for 15 minutes if you're sitting at a desk during travel.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper is where doubt creeps in. You're running 5–11 miles when you should be ready for 31 miles of Alpine terrain with 2,500m vert. This is normal and correct. Week 20–22 kills intensity but preserves neuromuscular sharpness and lets your aerobic system consolidate. The long run comes Saturday; that's when you'll feel alive again. Trust the plan. Your data is clean—no HRV suppression, heart rate stable, sleep crushing it.
